working_parent_changes.basis: Select James Glasgow-1970 of the Cookstown Mitchell family as John Glasgow-2539 of Gortin’s uncertain working father, through the existing possible identification with John Glasgow-1968. The 1879 Hillsdale history specifically identifies James and his Mitchell wife as parents of John, a farmer near Cookstown. The Gortin account supplies another John in the same Derryloran/Cookstown locality and an earlier compatible father generation. The maintained Hillsdale research already lists Gortin John as a possible duplicate. This is a positive named-son comparison in the relevant family and locality, stronger than an arbitrary father chosen only from the surname. Prefer this existing family as a revisable home for the 17-profile Gortin branch; retain both John accounts separately.
working_parent_changes.limitations: The identity is uncertain. The Hillsdale histories describe John and Jane’s seven children as Robert, Mary A., William, John, Bessie, James and Margaret; the Gortin account instead links Francis, Hugh, Letitia and Samuel. No child has been matched across those sets. An earlier union could explain different couple-based lists, but none is established here and no additional marriage is invented. If the seven-child account was intended as an exhaustive lifetime list for John, the extra Gortin group would conflict with it. The Gortin before-1771 birth boundary comes from Samuel’s reported 1792 birth; the Hillsdale c.1778 father estimate is younger. Literal 1778 fatherhood of a 1792 child would be about 14 and is a serious constraint. These are reconstructed ages and estimates, not two original birth entries; both are retained, without silently shifting either date. Sarah MacNeece’s status as the Gortin man’s widow and Jane’s identity also require testing; no mother is transferred to Gortin John and no wife is added or replaced. Another local John, a collateral relationship, or different father remain alternatives. The 1700s and 1800s family accounts do not independently prove these two Johns identical.

working_parent_changes.basis: Select the older James Glasgow-1025 account as the Cookstown progenitor James Glasgow-1970’s uncertain working father, conditional on the existing Corvanaghan/Moneymore family model. The c.1700 and c.1730 estimates allow a father–son generation. James-1970 is already a surviving possible identity for the Cookstown-area Corvanaghan James-2988, whose selected working father is James-1025 through the separate Moneymore comparison. Extending that same unproved pedigree gives the Mitchell account a consistent, revisable place in the broader family. The district context comes from those Cookstown/Corvanaghan/Moneymore comparisons, not from the 1759 index. This is an inherited family hypothesis with no independent father record for the Mitchell progenitor.
working_parent_changes.limitations: No will, lease or baptism names the Cookstown James as the older James’s son. The reviewed PRONI detail says Drumcarn, County Tyrone, not Drumearn, and gives 17 January 1759 without age or kin; the modern profile identity and meaning of that date remain unresolved. It cannot corroborate Drumearn residence, a death date, or this father choice. The older and younger James accounts may themselves be duplicates rather than separate generations; if established, the father edge must collapse. The existing older pedigree and the Corvanaghan/Moneymore identity remain unproved. The 1879 history reports Scotland-to-Cookstown migration about 1750, while the older James’s profile is placed in Tyrone; neither a return journey nor that Scottish birthplace is established here. Multiple James and William householders appear in the 1740 Derryloran return, and two James men appear at Drumearn in 1766. William or another local father, a collateral link and a separate Scottish origin remain alternatives. Mary Harkness is not transferred to the Mitchell account, and Margaret Rutherford is not assigned as its mother. James-1970, James-2988, James-1024 and the older James-1025 remain separate possible overlapping reconstructions, not independently proved sons or households.

grade_changes.basis: Assess the Hillsdale record-defined core as probable: James Glasgow-1970 as John Glasgow-1968’s father, Unknown Mitchell as that John’s mother, and James and Mitchell as spouses. The 1879 account explicitly gives those relationships; the 1888 sketches identify the same John–Jane household through sons William and John, their seven-child group and Michigan history. These are detailed late family accounts, not contemporary Scottish or Irish birth/marriage entries. Conflicting Scottish versus Tyrone origins, c.1778 dating and 1844/1848 immigration years limit the life-history reconstruction. The family-role identification is still a justified probable inference, while exact dates and the new upstream/Gortin links remain weaker separate questions. The prior local grades were unknown with saved unmarked parent flags; no already-confident link is counted as a new upgrade.
